body: The 2026 festival opens Friday with a 16-page printed program I designed and coded. The board approved the cover, and it went to the printer. The same week I finished a separate awards program and a promo video that is live on YouTube.

I have worked with VAASF since at least 2022. My Drive holds the final programs and application sheets for 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. I now own the Webflow site, including the redesigned events schedule, and built the 2026 application that collected 92 to 94 entries.

The booklet is a Python script that fills HTML pages from the repertoire data and prints each to PDF, so a late schedule change is a data edit and a rebuild, not a rework of a layout file. Each page has guide-overlay proofs for checking margins. It replaced a first draft built in Canva.
Next: after the festival I plan to rebuild the site in code, with one application form that takes payment, so no entries are left without a payment. That is a plan, nothing is built yet.
What I learned: with a small nonprofit, the deadline is the design brief. Showing the board a real PDF by noon beat any amount of talking about options.
